evidence: Cic. Off. 1.101: cujus nōn possit causam probābilem reddere
terms.comment: Hāc dē causā, for this reason; multīs dē causīs, for many reasons (Traupman 368); sine causā, for no reason (Cic.). The reason why: causa cūr or quamobrem with the subjunctive (Lewis & Short). Often Latin simply gives the reason in a clause with quod or quia.
The reasoning behind a thing, the account one gives of it.

evidence: Cic. Fam. 14.4.4: nihil est quod tē moveat
Hor. Ep. 2.1.30: nōn est quod multa loquāmur

phrases.latin: nec vērō agere quicquam, cujus nōn possit causam probābilem reddere
phrases.english: and to do nothing for which one cannot give a sound reason

phrases.latin: nōn amō tē, Sabidī, nec possum dīcere quārē
phrases.english: I don’t like you, Sabidius, and I can’t say why

phrases.latin: is ad mē rescrīpsit petīvitque ut ratiōnem dīcerem cūr tertium ac nōn tertiō scrīpsissem
phrases.english: he wrote back and asked me to give my reason for writing “tertium” and not “tertiō”
there is no reason for you to be upset
